<Subject 1> is the dark-gray SF3000-style handheld console from the prior product segment and <Picture 1> through <Picture 4>, preserving its wide horizontal shell, centered screen, dual analog sticks, left directional controls, right ABXY buttons, SELECT and START buttons, top shoulder controls, and rear speaker grille.
<Subject 2> is the control and connectivity system shown in <Picture 1>: extension buttons, power button, Micro TF card slot, DC/OTG port, headphone jack, volume control, D-pad, analog stick, SELECT, START, and customizable function buttons.
<Subject 3> is the rear hardware configuration shown in <Picture 2>: L2 and R2 shoulder buttons, rear extension buttons, speaker grille, and two integrated fold-out stands.
<Subject 4> is the on-device settings interface from <Picture 3> and <Picture 4>, featuring clear sound, brightness, language, display, key-mapping, and reset controls.
<Subject 5> is the accessibility feature from <Picture 4>: support for 25 selectable interface languages.

detailed_description:
The target video is exactly 15 seconds long in 9:16 vertical format. It continues the previous premium minimalist product-ad language: a matte-black studio, dark reflective base, controlled blue-and-amber rim lighting, clean original interface graphics, and crisp short English typography. No hands, no people, no copied game artwork, no cluttered technical diagrams, and no changes to the console’s physical layout.

[Shot 1] The scene opens on <Subject 1> in a narrow top-edge profile, centered against black. The camera makes a slow lateral slide across the console’s upper edge as thin amber locator lines rise from <Subject 2>: “POWER,” “MICRO TF,” “DC / OTG,” “HEADPHONES,” and “VOLUME.” Each label appears briefly, then fades as the next one activates. The camera lowers into a front three-quarter view, revealing the D-pad, analog stick, SELECT, START, and ABXY controls in their correct fixed positions. A final blue outline traces the controls while clean text appears above: “CUSTOM BUTTON MAPPING.” Soft clicks follow each locator line; one decisive confirmation tone ends the shot.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.800, cut to the back of <Subject 1>. <Subject 3> is revealed by a slow rotation as the two integrated stands unfold smoothly from the rear shell and lock into place with two quiet mechanical snaps. The console settles at a comfortable display angle on the reflective surface, screen facing upward toward the viewer. A narrow blue light catches the R2 and L2 shoulder buttons while the rear speaker grille receives a subtle amber highlight. Minimal centered text reads: “BUILT-IN STAND.” The camera makes a restrained half-orbit, keeping the stand mechanism clearly visible.

[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut to a straight-on close-up of the upright console. Its screen shows <Subject 4>, an original clean dark settings interface with two large horizontal sliders: a speaker icon and “SOUND” on top, a sun icon and “BRIGHTNESS” below. The sound slider advances two steps with a light electronic chime; the brightness slider advances and the display becomes visibly clearer and more luminous without blooming. The console remains physically still. Text above the product reads: “TUNE YOUR PLAY.” Each adjustment produces a precise UI tick.

[Shot 4] At 00:10.300, the camera pushes toward the screen as the settings menu selects “LANGUAGE.” <Subject 5> is shown through a fast, legible carousel of language names: “ENGLISH,” “ESPANOL,” “FRANCAIS,” “DEUTSCH,” “ITALIANO,” “PORTUGUES,” “日本語,” and “中文.” The selected line lands on “ENGLISH,” then the menu resolves into a single clean statement: “25 LANGUAGES.” Blue selection highlights move with controlled, instant response; a sequence of light confirmation clicks matches the transitions.

[Shot 5] At 00:13.000, pull back to the final hero shot. <Subject 1> rests on its integrated stand in a centered three-quarter view, its display bright and crisp. The blue and amber rim lights return to opposite edges of the shell, visually matching the preceding product segment. All interface elements fade away except the final centered text: “SET UP. SWITCH. PLAY.” The camera completes a subtle push-in and holds perfectly steady until 00:15.000.

overall_soundscape:
Clean studio silence under controlled product sounds: small button clicks, a single confirmation tone, subtle port-callout ticks, two soft stand-lock snaps, precise menu-navigation clicks, and a restrained electronic display shimmer. No dialogue or environmental noise.

non_diegetic_music:
Continue the previous segment’s minimalist electronic score at 120 BPM. Use dry retro percussion, a quiet synth bass pulse, and restrained blue-toned arpeggios. Add a brief warm harmonic lift as the stand opens, then reduce to a clean sustained final note during the closing hero shot.
